inputs.text:
Let’s be completely clear about what is really happening here, because the establishment narrative wants to paint working people standing up for their rights as a threat to society. The Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU) has issued a one-month ultimatum to the federal government, demanding the conclusion of the long-delayed renegotiation of the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions. They are prepared to launch an indefinite nationwide strike if their demands are unmet. 

This isn't about a "collapse of discipline"—it’s about workers finally pushing back against institutional neglect and systemic inequality. Stemming right out of the union’s 54th National Executive Council resolutions, these workers are refusing to be exploited any longer by a system that chronically underfunds education and ignores labor rights. The real threat to our youth and to societal stability isn't the workers demanding justice; it's decades of government failure to honor basic agreements and respect the dignity of labor. When the powers-that-be refuse accountability and stall negotiations indefinitely, collective action and disruption become the only tools left for vulnerable groups to demand fairness. We need structural reform, not moralizing lectures directed at the working class.
